title: A potato price gap that outlasted modeled costs
summary: Agra → Vashi New Mumbai, January 2021: a ₹690 per quintal median price gap on 23 matched days. After modeled costs: ₹278 per quintal on the typical day.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for January 2021: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 23 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.
Modal prices may mix varieties and grades (mostly FAQ).
Costs are survey values and assumptions, not quotes.
OSRM car profile; truck route not verified.

scenes.headline: January 2021
scenes.caption: Agra sits in western Uttar Pradesh's cold-stored potato belt; Vashi supplies Mumbai.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 23 matched days, Agra reported a median ₹910 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹1,600 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹690/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹690 per quintal and was positive on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,270 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,270 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~15 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹273/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: ₹278 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes ₹129 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 21 of 23 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 21 of 23 days, averaging ₹279 per quintal; 2 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: Even under the stress test, the modeled median stayed positive. It is still a historical model, not proof a trade happened or would work today.

assumptions.value: scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹273/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days

conclusion: Even under the stress test, the modeled median stayed positive. It is still a historical model, not proof a trade happened or would work today.

title: The month potato prices fell across India
summary: In January 2021, the median potato market moved -40.6% in a month, 2.8 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 2.8σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for potato, across 630 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: January 2021
scenes.caption: Potato prices across 630 markets that reported in both December 2020 and January 2021.

scenes.headline: Median move -40.6%
scenes.caption: The typical market's potato price fell 40.6% in one month. 99% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 2.8× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 2.8 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Tripura
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 23 reporting markets in Tripura had a median change of -59.2%.

scenes.headline: Raigarh
scenes.caption: Raigarh (Chattisgarh), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹2,250 → ₹1,000 per quintal (-55.6%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

scenes.headline: March 2021

scenes.headline: Harvest price
scenes.caption: Agra's March 2021 median: ₹645 per quintal.

scenes.headline: The informed bet
scenes.caption: Using only the 7 earlier years, March→October had averaged +₹427. A rule-following trader would store.

scenes.headline: October 2021
scenes.caption: October median: ₹920, a change of +42.6%.

scenes.headline: Shrinkage and interest
scenes.caption: Allowing 7% loss and 12% a year interest for 7 months leaves a storage budget of ₹165 per quintal.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: Seven months of storage needed to cost less than ₹165 per quintal to break even. Cold-storage rents are not in our cited evidence, so AGRINET does not claim a profit.

title: The potato trade that looked profitable but wasn't
summary: Agra → Vashi New Mumbai, November 2021: a ₹310 per quintal median price gap on 22 matched days. After modeled costs: −₹132 per quintal on the typical day.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for November 2021: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 22 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.
Modal prices may mix varieties and grades (mostly FAQ).
Costs are survey values and assumptions, not quotes.
OSRM car profile; truck route not verified.

scenes.headline: November 2021
scenes.caption: Agra sits in western Uttar Pradesh's cold-stored potato belt; Vashi supplies Mumbai.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 22 matched days, Agra reported a median ₹1,300 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹1,600 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹310/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹310 per quintal and was positive on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,270 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,270 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~15 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹273/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: −₹132 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes −₹282 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 5 of 22 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 9 of 22 days, averaging −₹21 per quintal; 5 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: The ₹310 gap looked tempting, but on the typical day modeled costs absorbed it. A gap on a price board is not a margin.

assumptions.value: scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹273/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days

conclusion: The ₹310 gap looked tempting, but on the typical day modeled costs absorbed it. A gap on a price board is not a margin.
